newsitem.title: GERMANY: Schwarz Pharma, U.S. firm cooperate on heart drug.
newsitem.headline: Schwarz Pharma, U.S. firm cooperate on heart drug.

text.p: German drugs manufacturer Schwarz Pharma AG said on Tuesday it and U.S. company Lynx Therapeutics Inc planned to cooperate in the development and marketing of a new heart drug called LR-3280.

Under the agreement reached on Tuesday Schwarz Pharma will make a part payment of four million dollars to California-based Lynx plus further so-called "milestone" payments totalling a combined $16 million, Schwarz Pharma said in a statement.
The German company will also bear the cost of development, the statement said.
A spokesman for Schwarz Pharma said development costs were estimated at $60 to $70 million if the project proceeded well. Both Lynx and Schwarz Pharma would conduct research and development, he said.
The companies plan to launch the drug in the year 2003, the spokesman said. "But that's just a planned date. It could be 2005, or if things go well, 2002," the spokesman said.

The drug, to be launched in Europe and North America, aims to prevent the reclosure of coronary blood vessels by manipulating genes which are responsible for the excessive regeneration of cells inside arteries following balloon treatment with heart catheters to widen narrowed vessels.
This cell regeneration, akin to scar tissue, leads to a renarrowing of coronary vessels in 30 to 50 percent of patients undergoing heart catheter treatment, Schwarz Pharma said.
